title: "socioeconomic_score"

We want to clean the socieconomic factor provided by SOA
Raw file is accessed from https://www.soa.org/resources/research-reports/2020/us-mort-rate-socioeconomic/#excel


```{r}
rm(list=ls());gc()
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)

sis_2005_2009 <- read_excel("mort-socioeconomic-country-level.xlsx", 
    sheet = "2005-2009 ACS", skip = 2) |> select(State_USPS, Source, Score, Total_Pop)

sis_2010_2014 <- read_excel("mort-socioeconomic-country-level.xlsx", 
    sheet = "2010-2014 ACS", skip = 2) |> select(State_USPS, Source, Score, Total_Pop)

sis_2015_2019 <- read_excel("mort-socioeconomic-country-level.xlsx", 
    sheet = "2015-2019 ACS", skip = 2) |> select(State_USPS, Source, Score, Total_Pop)


```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)

# =========================================================
# 1) State -> Census region/division crosswalk (50 states + DC)
# =========================================================
state_census_xwalk <- tibble::tribble(
  ~State_USPS, ~Census_Region, ~Census_Division,
  "CT","Northeast","New England",
  "ME","Northeast","New England",
  "MA","Northeast","New England",
  "NH","Northeast","New England",
  "RI","Northeast","New England",
  "VT","Northeast","New England",

  "NJ","Northeast","Middle Atlantic",
  "NY","Northeast","Middle Atlantic",
  "PA","Northeast","Middle Atlantic",

  "IL","Midwest","East North Central",
  "IN","Midwest","East North Central",
  "MI","Midwest","East North Central",
  "OH","Midwest","East North Central",
  "WI","Midwest","East North Central",

  "IA","Midwest","West North Central",
  "KS","Midwest","West North Central",
  "MN","Midwest","West North Central",
  "MO","Midwest","West North Central",
  "NE","Midwest","West North Central",
  "ND","Midwest","West North Central",
  "SD","Midwest","West North Central",

  "DE","South","South Atlantic",
  "DC","South","South Atlantic",
  "FL","South","South Atlantic",
  "GA","South","South Atlantic",
  "MD","South","South Atlantic",
  "NC","South","South Atlantic",
  "SC","South","South Atlantic",
  "VA","South","South Atlantic",
  "WV","South","South Atlantic",

  "AL","South","East South Central",
  "KY","South","East South Central",
  "MS","South","East South Central",
  "TN","South","East South Central",

  "AR","South","West South Central",
  "LA","South","West South Central",
  "OK","South","West South Central",
  "TX","South","West South Central",

  "AZ","West","Mountain",
  "CO","West","Mountain",
  "ID","West","Mountain",
  "MT","West","Mountain",
  "NV","West","Mountain",
  "NM","West","Mountain",
  "UT","West","Mountain",
  "WY","West","Mountain",

  "AK","West","Pacific",
  "CA","West","Pacific",
  "HI","West","Pacific",
  "OR","West","Pacific",
  "WA","West","Pacific"
)

# =========================================================
# 2) Weighted mean helper (Score weighted by Total_Pop)
# =========================================================
wtd_mean <- function(x, w) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w) & w > 0
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(x[ok] * w[ok]) / sum(w[ok])
}

# =========================================================
# 3) Stack your three SIS tables (keeps Source as-is)
#    key fix #1: parse numbers robustly (commas, etc.)
# =========================================================
sis_all <- bind_rows(
  sis_2005_2009,
  sis_2010_2014,
  sis_2015_2019
) %>%
  mutate(
    State_USPS = toupper(trimws(State_USPS)),
    Total_Pop  = readr::parse_number(as.character(Total_Pop)),
    Score      = readr::parse_number(as.character(Score))
  )

# Optional: quick check for states not in crosswalk
missing_states <- sis_all %>%
  distinct(State_USPS) %>%
  anti_join(state_census_xwalk, by = "State_USPS")

# Optional: quick check for numeric parsing problems
# sis_all %>% summarise(
#   n = n(),
#   pop_na = sum(is.na(Total_Pop)),
#   score_na = sum(is.na(Score))
# )

# =========================================================
# 4) Join to region/division and aggregate
# =========================================================
sis_tagged <- sis_all %>%
  inner_join(state_census_xwalk, by = "State_USPS")

# key fix #2: compute Score BEFORE Total_Pop inside summarise
# (dplyr summarise evaluates left-to-right; otherwise Total_Pop becomes a scalar and can break weighting)

# 4a) Census division level
sis_division <- sis_tagged %>%
  group_by(Source, Census_Region, Census_Division) %>%
  summarise(
    Score     = wtd_mean(Score, Total_Pop),
    Total_Pop = sum(Total_Pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Source, Census_Region, Census_Division)

# 4b) Census region level
sis_region <- sis_tagged %>%
  group_by(Source, Census_Region) %>%
  summarise(
    Score     = wtd_mean(Score, Total_Pop),
    Total_Pop = sum(Total_Pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Source, Census_Region)

# Optional: identify groups that still have NA Score (usually because all weights are NA/0)
# sis_division %>% filter(is.na(Score) | Total_Pop == 0)
# sis_region   %>% filter(is.na(Score) | Total_Pop == 0)

# =========================================================
# 5) Outputs
# =========================================================
sis_division_final <- sis_division  |> mutate(
    start_year = as.integer(str_extract(Source, "^\\d{4}")),
    end_year   = as.integer(str_extract(Source, "(?<=-)\\d{4}"))
  )|> select(-Total_Pop, -Source)

sis_region_final <- sis_region  |> mutate(
    start_year = as.integer(str_extract(Source, "^\\d{4}")),
    end_year   = as.integer(str_extract(Source, "(?<=-)\\d{4}"))
  )|> select(-Total_Pop, -Source)


sis_division_final |> select(-Census_Region) |> write_csv("covariate_socioeconomic_score_division.csv")
sis_region_final |> write_csv("covariate_socioeconomic_score_region.csv")
```
